messages.subject: Custom log_ method
parts:
Hi, 

I am doing a simulation where real datetime objects are being used and converted to integer so that simmer can work with these date times. So, I am using the time represented as seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC. 

Now when doing a simulation I would like to log the real time stamps. I have tried using the following: 

datetimeformat = stamp("Sun 2018-08-17 11:12:13")

secondsToDateTime = function(seconds) { 
  as.POSIXct(seconds, origin = "1970-01-01", tz= "UTC")
}

# dtlog function to log the date and time instead of seconds since 1970-01-01
dtlog = function(trajectory, text, level = 2) { 
  # log with the date time in UTC (same timezone as in dataset)
  log_(trajectory, function() {
           paste0(now(env), ' ', datetimeformat(secondsToDateTime(now(env))),
                  ' ', text)
    }, level)
  trajectory
}

Now this works when env is defined in the scope of the dtlog function but it no longer works (unsurprisingly) works when the env object is not found in the scope. 

How can I write a custom log_ function that does the appropriate formatting? Is there a generic way to access the env object from the trajectory? 

Cheers
  Erik

messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Re: Custom log_ method
parts:
On Sun, 27 Jan 2019 at 21:58, Erik Brakkee <erik.b...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Adding an 'env' object to the global environmnet is a work around. Is there a way in R to call a function and explicitly add a variable to the scope of a function? In that case I can explicitly pass an object named 'env' to the function that create the trajectory.

It's not a workaround, but the way to go. A simmer environment is just
a pointer to a C++ object (plus some methods to work with it), so the
only important thing is that it should be available in some parent
environment when a trajectory uses it. That's why one of our
recommended best practices (see section 4.3 in [1]) is to instantiate
the environment in the first place, e.g.,

env <- simmer()

traj <- trajectory() %>%
log_(function() paste0("Current simulation time: ", now(env)))

env <- env %>%
add_generator("dummy", traj, at(rexp(1, 1))) %>%
run()

The code is more readable and some potential mistakes are avoided.

Iñaki

[1] https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-02-jss.pdf
